title: Jebena coffee brewing
summary: In Ethiopia and Eritrea coffee is made fresh from green beans: roasted in a flat pan over charcoal, pounded in a wooden mortar, boiled in a round-bellied clay pot and poured from a height into a row of small cups.
howToPlay: Roast: drag round and round in the pan to turn the beans, then pull the pan when the colour reaches the green band.
Pound: tap as the ring closes on the mouth of the mortar.
Boil: fan the charcoal or set the pot aside to keep the brew in the green band of the neck window without overflowing.
Pour: press and hold, sweep slowly along the cups with the spout held high, and bring every cup to the same level.
rules: Each step is scored; press the lit button to finish a step.
Beans left on the hot place of the pan go dark first.
Taps off the beat make the beans jump out of the mortar.
Never let the brew rise past the red mark in the neck.
A shaky pour, or the last grounds from the pot, cloud the cups.
heritageNote: Across Ethiopia and Eritrea, coffee is a daily household craft. Villages often favour their own shape of jebena, a clay pot with a narrow neck that holds back the grounds as the coffee is poured. The skill lies in judging colour, sound and aroma at every step.
